summary: The most likely root cause of INC-009 is the portfolio-service v4.5.0 deployment at 2026-05-05T08:56:00Z, whose new, unindexed query 'SELECT * FROM trades WHERE account_id=$1 AND executed_at > $2 ORDER BY executed_at' performs a 48.2M-row Seq Scan on the shared ledger-db instance, saturating its CPU/connections and starving order-service's INSERTs into statement-timeout failures (H1, confidence 0.72, medium). Onset is established at the 08:48–08:56Z bucket from four independent signals (order-service p99 and 5xx, ledger-db CPU/connections/slow_queries), and the DB-side slow-query population is 100% portfolio-service's Seq Scan with zero occurrences before 08:58:38Z; the only cleanly ordered pair is 08:58:38Z (first portfolio Seq Scan) → 09:00:42Z (first order-service statement timeout). The competing hypotheses are closed or contradicted: the DBA autovacuum change is excluded on mechanism and timing (autovacuum only ever touches audit_log; a 48–56 min flat gap after 08:00Z), no storage/host/maintenance event exists in the change inventory, and order-service's own resources were flat with its pool rising only with the latency jump. Confidence is held below high because two load-bearing sub-details remain assumptions rather than verified facts — that v4.5.0 introduced a genuinely new unindexed query (vs. a plan regression at the same instant) and whether the binding shared resource is CPU/IO or pooled connections — but both collapse to the same origin and the same fix family, so they cap confidence without creating a competing origin.

ranked_hypotheses.title: portfolio-service v4.5.0's new unindexed trades query saturates shared ledger-db, starving order-service writes
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The portfolio-service v4.5.0 deployment at 2026-05-05T08:56:00Z introduced the query 'SELECT * FROM trades WHERE account_id=$1 AND executed_at > $2 ORDER BY executed_at' with no supporting index ('no migration included'). On the shared ledger-db instance this query performs a Seq Scan over 48.2M rows, driving ledger-db CPU ~30%->~96%, connections_active ~61->~190 and slow_queries ~1/min->~140/min. ledger-db is shared by four db callers, so order-service's INSERT INTO orders statements lose the CPU/IO (or pooled-connection) budget, exceed statement_timeout and fail, giving p99 ~5.4s and ~9.6% 5xx. The fault originates in the portfolio-service release, not in order-service or the DB config. NOTE: whether the fault is a genuinely new unindexed query or a pre-existing query whose plan regressed at the same moment is an open sub-detail (same origin, same fix family: add index / revert release); whether the binding shared resource is CPU/IO or pooled connections is likewise an open sub-detail (same origin, remediation shifts to pooler/limit tuning). Neither sub-detail changes the origin.

causal_chain.claim: portfolio-service v4.5.0 deploys at 2026-05-05T08:56:00Z adding 'a new query on trades filtered by account_id + executed_at' with explicitly 'no migration included' (no index added); it is the only service-side change in the whole window and was never rolled back.

That exact query is the sole content of ledger-db's slow-query log: all 360 WARN lines are 'SELECT * FROM trades WHERE account_id=$n AND executed_at > $n ORDER BY executed_at -- Seq Scan on trades (rows=48211907)' with application_name=portfolio-service, first at 08:58:38Z; no slow query from order-service/payment/settlement appears.

The query/plan is absent before the deploy: zero Seq Scan lines anywhere in 06:00-08:58:39Z other than the 08:58:38Z first occurrence, and the per-minute count switches from exact zero across every minute 06:00-08:56Z to a steady multi-per-minute plateau (1,2,4,4,3,3,3,2,4,2,3,5,1,3...) from 08:58Z onward; the plan shape is stable Seq Scan in all 360 lines with no recorded plan transition.

ASSUMED sub-detail: the Seq Scan appears because v4.5.0 introduced a genuinely new unindexed query, rather than a pre-existing query whose plan regressed / index was dropped-bypassed at the same instant. The logs expose no index name, no DDL (zero 'CREATE INDEX'/'INDEX' matches in 06:00-11:00Z) and no pre-deploy baseline plan for this pattern, so this cannot be separated from telemetry; either way the trigger is the release.
The 48.2M-row scan on the shared instance drives ledger-db CPU ~30%->~96%, connections_active ~61->~190, slow_queries ~1/min->~140/min, all with the same 08:48-08:56Z onset bucket.

ledger-db is a shared=true postgres with four direct db callers (order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service, settlement-service) and no intermediate pooler/proxy node in its topology, so portfolio-service's change and order-service's writes are on the same shared dependency path; contention between reads and order-service writes is structural.

ASSUMED sub-detail: the binding shared resource is CPU/IO budget (scan starving writes), as opposed to pooled-connection count. No ledger-db max_connections, no pooler config and no configured pool-size denominator for either caller exists in the record, so 'CPU starvation' vs 'shared pool exhaustion' is unresolvable; both are downstream of the same portfolio-service origin.

order-service's only error signature is statement timeout on writes against ledger-db ('canceling statement due to statement timeout (INSERT INTO orders)', 284 ERROR matches, first 09:00:42Z, ~2 min after portfolio-service's first slow query at 08:58:38Z); its CPU stays flat (~39.8-40.7%) and its pool fills only from the same onset bucket, i.e. it is blocked on the shared DB, not compute-saturated.

order-service p99 jumps ~150ms -> 3.4-5.6s and 5xx ~0.2% -> ~9.6% in the 08:48-08:56Z onset bucket, and portfolio-service p99 rises in the same bucket (177ms -> ~6.8-7.0s) with its pool pinned at its 50-connection ceiling while its CPU stays flat - the same 'blocked on blocked statements with idle CPU' signature, corroborating a shared dependency degrading both callers.

Structural precedent: HIST-111 (2025-05-22) 'Reporting job full table scans slowed ledger-db', root cause 'New report query without index did sequential scans', resolution 'Added index; query review gate' - a near-exact structural match to the observed pattern.

assumptions: Sub-detail A (load-bearing, unresolved): the Seq Scan stems from a truly new query in v4.5.0 rather than a plan regression / index drop at the same moment. Supported only by 'no migration included' plus total absence of any prior occurrence of this pattern; no catalog/index state and no pre-deploy baseline plan exist in telemetry.

Sub-detail B (load-bearing, unresolved): portfolio-service reads and order-service writes contend on the same ledger-db budget, and the binding resource is CPU/IO rather than pooled connections. Established as topology (shared=true, four callers, no pooler node) but not measured as contention; ledger-db max_connections and per-service pool sizes are unknown.

Timing caveat: the deploy timestamp (08:56:00Z) sits at the RIGHT EDGE of the 08:48-08:56Z onset bucket and the first rising sample is in that same bucket; the first Seq Scan log (08:58:38Z) follows it. The only cleanly ordered pair is 08:58:38Z (portfolio Seq Scan) -> 09:00:42Z (order-service timeout). 'Deploy precedes onset' is therefore bucket-granular, not sample-granular.

Blast radius is asserted from topology, not measured: payment-service and settlement-service (the other two db callers) were never checked at the app layer, and portfolio-service shows latency-only degradation (error_rate flat ~0.2%), so the measured app-layer blast radius is one 5xx victim plus one latency-only victim.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Storage/IOPS infrastructure degradation on the ledger-db host coinciding with (not caused by) the change window
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The ledger-db host's underlying storage (cloud volume burst credits / IOPS) degraded independently, throttling I/O on the shared instance; the CPU, connection and slow-query saturation and order-service statement timeouts are downstream of that storage fault. HIST-110 (2026-01-15) had a near-identical symptom set (order latency + ledger-db statement timeouts).

causal_chain.claim: Cloud volume burst credits on the ledger-db host are exhausted / IOPS throttled (no finding - pure lead from HIST-110 precedent).
I/O throttling would slow the trades scan and order-service inserts, raising CPU/connections/slow queries from the 08:56Z bucket. This is consistent with the observed saturation.
order-service INSERT INTO orders statements hit statement_timeout, giving p99 ~5.4s and ~9.6% 5xx.

But no storage-tier event exists anywhere: the change inventory contains only the autovacuum config change and the portfolio deploy, with no IOPS provisioning change, disk resize, host/DB maintenance entry or storage-tier migration; ledger-db's dependency graph has no storage/host/volume node; and replication_lag_ms is flat ~39-43ms across the window.

More fundamentally, a storage fault is not needed: 100% of DB-side slow-query volume and the exact onset are attributable to one new portfolio-service Seq Scan appearing immediately after the deploy, with zero occurrences before it.

assumptions: Storage-tier throttling occurred without any change on the board - the change inventory covered deployments and config changes (plus a negative 18h sweep) only, so an infra/maintenance event source outside those APIs is not proven absent.

IOPS/disk-latency metrics for ledger-db are absent from telemetry, so the mechanism cannot be directly confirmed or fully excluded; it ranks low because the single new portfolio-service query fully explains the DB-side evidence without invoking storage throttling.

ranked_hypotheses.title: DBA autovacuum setting change on ledger-db (scale_factor 0.2 -> 0.1) caused bloat/lock/IO contention
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The reporter's suspicion: the ledger-db autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor change at 2026-05-05T08:00:00Z by dba-team ('More aggressive autovacuum') made autovacuum run harder on the large trades table, consuming CPU/IO and/or taking locks, degrading ledger-db generally and surfacing as order-service statement timeouts.

causal_chain.claim: DBA changes autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2 -> 0.1 on ledger-db at 08:00:00Z ('More aggressive autovacuum'); cfg-2903 is confirmed applied at 08:00:20Z.
More aggressive autovacuum would have to fire on the trades table and hold IO/CPU or locks for ~48-56 minutes before onset, with no intermediate signal.

Autovacuum on ledger-db is entirely on public.audit_log, never on trades: no autovacuum line, lock or bloat signal names trades; cadence is similar before and after 08:00Z; no autovacuum event at 08:56-08:58Z.
There is no autovacuum/verbose WARN activity in the pre-onset window at all - only one unrelated clock-drift line at 06:44:41Z - so no autovacuum-induced lock/bloat/slow query precedes onset.
Every DB-side slow query in the window is the portfolio-service Seq Scan on trades, not vacuum/lock activity and not any order-service query.
ledger-db CPU/connections/slow_queries rise only from the 08:48-08:56Z bucket, ~48-56 min after the config change across a flat gap.

assumptions: Autovacuum on trades could not be directly observed because ledger-db exposes no vacuum/dead-tuple/IO/lock metric (available_metrics: connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min), so the mechanism is untestable in principle rather than affirmatively disproven at the metric level; the log evidence (F25, F26) is what closes it.

A residual non-actionable possibility remains that autovacuum load contributes some background pressure, but no log evidence ties any DB-side symptom to vacuum activity and it would not change the fix.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Closed on both mechanism and timing. (1) Mechanism: every autovacuum INFO line on ledger-db names public.audit_log, never trades; no lock, bloat or vacuum signal mentions trades; the run cadence is the same before and after 08:00Z; and there is no autovacuum event at 08:56-08:58Z (F25, F26). (2) Timing: the config change precedes onset by ~48-56 minutes across a completely flat gap, with only a single unrelated clock-drift WARN in the pre-onset window (F15, F26). (3) Symptom attribution: 100% of DB-side slow queries are portfolio-service's new Seq Scan, first appearing 58 minutes AFTER the config change and immediately after the deploy - a pattern the config change cannot produce (F10, F21, F22). No historical precedent exists for an autovacuum-caused outage (F18).

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service's own resource exhaustion (connection/thread pool saturation) making it slow to issue ledger-db statements
ranked_hypotheses.statement: order-service itself exhausted its DB connection pool or thread pool without any release, so requests queued and statements timed out client-side; ledger-db's CPU/connection/slow-query rise is a consequence of order-service's own churn or an independent side effect.

causal_chain.claim: order-service db/thread pool in use rises and saturates before the DB saturation.
Queued requests spend >5s before/while writing, producing statement timeouts on INSERT INTO orders, giving p99 ~5.4s and ~9.6% 5xx.
Consequent stack-ups would raise ledger-db connections_active and CPU.

But order-service has no release this week, its CPU is flat, and its pool fill (14 -> ~45) and the latency jump occur in the SAME bucket, not before - no pre-onset pool saturation; its first timeout (09:00:42Z) occurs ~2 min AFTER portfolio-service's first DB slow query (08:58:38Z), so order-service reacts to the DB, not the reverse.

assumptions: Client-side queueing would not necessarily produce DB-side slow queries, so F10's 'no order-service slow queries' does not fully exclude this; no GC-pause, heap, thread-pool or worker metric exists for order-service, so a thread-pool variant is unmeasurable.

A restart-driven variant (pod restart at onset) remains unchecked because memory_pct/restarts were never retrieved; this does not threaten the ranking because the DB-side slow queries are 100% portfolio-service.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: order-service CPU is flat at ~39.8-40.7% across the whole window including the onset bucket; its db_pool_in_use rises in the SAME bucket as the latency jump (F28, F29) rather than before it, so there is no pre-onset pool saturation; and no order-service release/config change exists in the window (F4, F17). Above all, the DB-side slow-query population is 100% portfolio-service's Seq Scan with zero order-service slow queries (F10, F21), so order-service is a victim, not the pressure source.

facts.statement: Across all services, exactly one deployment occurred in the 06:00-10:00Z window (and in the wider 2026-05-04T12:00-09:10Z sweep): portfolio-service v4.5.0 at 2026-05-05T08:56:00Z by k.shah, described as 'Add realised P&L breakdown to holdings API' with a 'new query on trades filtered by account_id + executed_at' and 'no migration included'; status live, never rolled back.

Across all services, exactly one config change occurred in the window: ledger-db 'autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor' changed from 0.2 to 0.1 at 2026-05-05T08:00:00Z by dba-team ('More aggressive autovacuum'). No connection-pool size, statement_timeout, or timeout config change was returned for any service.

An 18h pre-window sweep (2026-05-04T12:00Z to 2026-05-05T06:00Z) returned zero deployments and zero config changes, so the autovacuum change (08:00Z) and portfolio-service v4.5.0 (08:56Z) are the only two changes on the board.
ledger-db is a shared postgres datastore (shared=true) with four direct 'db' callers: order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service.

order-service's dependency surface contains no changed node: its edges are ledger-db (db), pricing-engine (http), exchange-gateway (http) and kafka (queue-produce); there is no code/service deployment edge for order-service in the window, consistent with the report that it has not been released this week.
order-service p99 latency was flat at ~147-153ms until the 08:48-08:56Z bucket, then jumped to avg 3368.94ms / max 5607.8ms at 08:56:00Z and stayed ~5.0-5.4s through the end of data.
order-service error_rate was 0.19-0.26% until 08:48Z, then rose to avg 4.7% / max 9.6% in the 08:56Z bucket and held ~9.2-9.6% for the rest of the window.

ledger-db CPU was ~29-30% until 08:48Z, then jumped to avg 79.56% / max 96.81% at 08:56Z and held ~95-96%; connections_active rose in the same bucket from ~61 to avg 156.11 / max 199.81 (later ~188-198); slow_queries_per_min rose from ~1/min to avg 106.94 / max 148.81 in the same bucket (later ~138-142/min).

All 360 of ledger-db's WARN slow-query lines in the window have the identical pattern 'SELECT * FROM trades WHERE account_id=$1 AND executed_at > $2 ORDER BY executed_at -- Seq Scan on trades (rows=48211907)' with application_name=portfolio-service; the first is at 08:58:38Z and no slow-query line from any other application_name appears.

The earliest occurrence of any 'SELECT * FROM trades ... Seq Scan on trades' line is 2026-05-05T08:58:38Z; a targeted query restricted to 06:00:00Z-08:58:39Z returned only that single line, so zero Seq Scan lines occurred before 08:56:00Z.

Per-minute counts of the portfolio-service Seq Scan line were zero for every minute 06:00-08:56Z, then switched immediately to a steady multi-per-minute plateau from 08:58Z onward (e.g. 08:58Z=1, 09:00Z=4, 09:09Z=5), totalling 360 over ~120 minutes after onset.

order-service's dominant and only error signature is statement timeout on writes: 'ledger-db: canceling statement due to statement timeout (INSERT INTO orders) orderId=<n>' — 284 ERROR matches, one pattern, first_seen 2026-05-05T09:00:42Z, which is ~2 minutes after portfolio-service's first slow query at 08:58:38Z.

Onset of all four first-rising samples (order-service p99, error_rate, ledger-db CPU/connections/slow_queries) is the 08:48-08:56Z bucket; the autovacuum change at 08:00Z precedes onset by ~48-56 minutes with a long flat gap, whereas the portfolio-service deployment is timestamped 08:56:00Z inside the onset bucket, with the first DB-side slow query at 08:58:38Z.

Autovacuum activity on ledger-db is entirely on public.audit_log, never on trades: all 20 'autovacuum: processed table public.audit_log' INFO lines (first 06:30:57Z, last 10:55:51Z) name audit_log, run cadence is similar before and after 08:00Z, and there is no autovacuum event at 08:56-08:58Z.

No autovacuum/verbose WARN activity exists on ledger-db in the pre-onset window: WARN logs 06:00:00-08:56:00Z returned a single unrelated 'clock drift 38ms detected, resyncing with NTP' at 06:44:41Z and nothing else.
order-service CPU_pct was flat across the whole window, including the onset bucket: 06:00-08:45Z averaged 39.84-40.69% and the 09:00Z bucket averaged 39.8% / max 41.75%.

order-service db_pool_in_use was flat at ~13.84-14.4 until 08:30Z, then rose in the SAME bucket as the latency jump (08:45Z avg 15.89 / max 45.07), then sat ~44.9-46.5 (max 51.63) — no pre-existing pool saturation.

portfolio-service latency_p99 rose in the same 08:45-09:00Z bucket as order-service (baseline ~177-182ms, then avg 1086.06ms / max 7056.7ms at 08:45Z and ~6838-6981ms for the rest), corroborating a shared dependency degrading both callers simultaneously.
portfolio-service's HTTP error_rate did NOT rise at onset, holding 0.18-0.24% across the entire window, so the 5xx blast radius is confined to order-service.

portfolio-service db_pool_in_use rose in the same bucket and pinned at exactly its 50-connection ceiling (avg=50 max=50 for every bucket 09:00Z-10:45Z) while its CPU_pct stayed flat at ~35.5-36.6% — the same blocked-statement signature as order-service.
ledger-db replication_lag_ms stayed flat at ~39-41ms across the whole window with no change at onset, so replication lag is not part of the degradation.

No index-maintenance evidence exists on ledger-db for the incident window: searches in 06:00-11:00Z for contains='CREATE INDEX' and contains='INDEX' (and for INFO lines containing 'index') each returned total_matched=0, so no index was created or dropped at or around 08:56Z.

The log evidence is consistent with a NEW query rather than a pre-existing query whose plan regressed: the Seq Scan pattern is absent before 08:56:00Z and is never logged as an Index Scan before and Seq Scan after — no plan-change transition is recorded anywhere.

ledger-db has no catalog/index telemetry at all — its available_metrics list is exactly ['connections_active','cpu_pct','disk_used_pct','replication_lag_ms','slow_queries_per_min'] — so DB-side index usage cannot be measured by any metric query.

ledger-db's dependency graph contains no connection pooler, proxy or middleware node: its neighbours are exactly the four direct db callers plus api-gateway http edges, and each caller has a direct 'kind':'db' edge.

A config-change sweep over all services from 2026-01-01 to 2026-05-05T11:00Z returned exactly one change, cfg-2903 on ledger-db (autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2 -> 0.1); no max_connections, pool_size, pgbouncer or statement_timeout entry exists in the change record.

The 06:00-11:00Z change inventory contains no storage/infrastructure/maintenance event: no IOPS provisioning change, disk resize, host/database maintenance entry, or storage-tier migration in the window.

Historical precedent relevant to H1: HIST-111 (2025-05-22) 'Reporting job full table scans slowed ledger-db' had root cause 'New report query without index did sequential scans' and resolution 'Added index; query review gate' — a near-exact structural match to the observed portfolio-service query pattern.

Historical precedent HIST-110 (2026-01-15) 'Slow orders from ledger-db IOPS throttling' had a near-identical symptom set (order latency, statement timeouts, slow queries) but a different stated cause (cloud volume burst credits exhausted) and resolution (moved to provisioned IOPS).
No historical incident mentioning autovacuum as a cause was returned by either the generic or ledger-db-scoped precedent search.

assumptions: Sub-detail A (load-bearing, unresolved): the Seq Scan stems from a genuinely NEW unindexed query introduced by v4.5.0 rather than a pre-existing query whose plan regressed or whose index was dropped/became unusable at the same moment. This is supported only by 'no migration included', the total absence of the pattern before 08:56Z, and the complete absence of index DDL in the logs; ledger-db exposes no catalog/index telemetry and log retention (05:00Z floor) prevents a true pre-deploy baseline, so this cannot be affirmatively proven.

Sub-detail B (load-bearing, unresolved): portfolio-service reads and order-service writes contend on the same ledger-db resource budget, and the binding resource is CPU/IO rather than pooled connections. Established as topology (shared=true, four direct callers, no pooler node) but not measured as contention; ledger-db max_connections and configured per-service pool sizes are unobtainable.

Timing is bucket-granular, not sample-granular: the deploy timestamp (08:56:00Z) sits at the RIGHT EDGE of the 08:48-08:56Z onset bucket and the first rising sample is in that same bucket, so 'deploy precedes onset' is bucket-granular only. The only cleanly ordered pair is 08:58:38Z (portfolio Seq Scan) -> 09:00:42Z (order-service timeout).

Blast radius is asserted from topology rather than measured: payment-service and settlement-service were never checked at the app layer, and portfolio-service shows latency-only degradation (error_rate flat ~0.2%), so the app-layer blast radius actually measured is one 5xx victim (order-service) plus one latency-only victim (portfolio-service).

The pool '50-connection ceiling' for portfolio-service (and the ~50-ish figure for order-service) is inferred from db_pool_in_use pinning at exactly max=50.0, not read from a configured size metric (no db_pool_size metric exists and no pool_size config entry was found), so pool saturation is asserted from the plateau rather than from a utilization ratio.

'No index-maintenance evidence in five days' should be read as 'none in 2026-05-05T05:00Z-10:59Z': the log store's data_range start is 2026-05-05T05:00:00Z regardless of requested start, so an index created or dropped before 05:00Z on 2026-05-05 cannot be ruled out.

The absence of a documented connection pooler, storage event, or maintenance entry is absence from the deployment/config/topology APIs only; it is not affirmative proof that no pooler, feature-flag change, migration job, or infra/maintenance event existed outside those APIs.

timeline.event: DBA config change cfg-2903 applied on ledger-db: autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2 -> 0.1 ('More aggressive autovacuum'). This is one of only two changes in the window; it precedes onset by ~48-56 minutes across a flat gap.
Log confirms 'config change cfg-2903 applied: autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor=0.1'. Autovacuum cadence afterwards remains similar to before and continues to touch only public.audit_log.
Start of the onset bucket: order-service p99, error_rate, ledger-db CPU/connections/slow_queries all still at baseline in the bucket ending 08:48Z, then rise in the bucket ending 08:56Z.

portfolio-service v4.5.0 deployed by k.shah ('Add realised P&L breakdown to holdings API'), introducing 'SELECT * FROM trades WHERE account_id=$1 AND executed_at > $2 ORDER BY executed_at' with 'no migration included'; status live, never rolled back. Onset bucket also contains the first rising samples for order-service p99/error_rate and ledger-db CPU (~79.56% avg / 96.81% max), connections_active (~156 avg) and slow_queries (~107/min avg).

First ledger-db WARN slow query: portfolio-service's 'SELECT * FROM trades ... Seq Scan on trades (rows=48211907)' at 8690ms. Zero occurrences of this pattern exist before this instant. Per-minute counts then plateau (08:58Z=1, 08:59Z=2, 09:00Z=4 ...).
First order-service statement-timeout ERROR: 'ledger-db: canceling statement due to statement timeout (INSERT INTO orders) orderId=<n>' — ~2 minutes after the first portfolio-service slow query.

order-service error_rate reaches ~9.2-9.6% and holds; order-service db_pool_in_use sits ~44.9-46.5 (max 51.63) while its CPU stays flat at ~39.8%; portfolio-service pool pins at exactly 50 with CPU flat ~35.5-36.6%; portfolio-service error_rate remains flat at ~0.2% (latency-only degradation).

Incident reported by on-call SRE: order-service p99 > 5s with statement timeouts against ledger-db; reporter notes order-service has not been released this week and the DBA changed autovacuum settings this morning.

Last matched Seq Scan slow-query line; the 360-line population over ~120 minutes remains 100% portfolio-service's single normalized pattern, and order-service p99 remains ~5.4s with error_rate ~9.65% at the end of data.

recommended_actions.action: Immediately roll back / disable the portfolio-service v4.5.0 deployment (change tc-006, 'Add realised P&L breakdown to holdings API', status live, never rolled back), reverting the holdings API to the pre-v4.5.0 code path that does not issue the trades Seq Scan query.
recommended_actions.rationale: The 360-line DB slow-query population is 100% portfolio-service's 48.2M-row Seq Scan that appears only after this deploy, and the only cleanly ordered pair is 08:58:38Z (first portfolio slow query) -> 09:00:42Z (first order-service timeout). Reverting removes the load source and should restore ledger-db CPU/connections and order-service p99/5xx.

recommended_actions.action: If rollback is not immediately possible, add a supporting index on trades(account_id, executed_at) on ledger-db (CONCURRENTLY to avoid lock impact) as a hotfix, then verify the plan changes from Seq Scan to Index Scan.
recommended_actions.rationale: The observed query filters on account_id + executed_at and orders by executed_at, and scans 48.2M rows with no supporting index; HIST-111 (a near-exact structural match) was resolved by 'Added index'. This is the same fix family as rollback and is the durable fix if the feature is kept.

recommended_actions.action: Verify recovery after rollback/index: confirm order-service p99 returns to ~147-153ms and 5xx to ~0.2%, ledger-db CPU back to ~30%, connections_active back to ~61, and slow_queries_per_min back toward ~1/min; confirm the portfolio-service Seq Scan line stops appearing.
recommended_actions.rationale: These are the exact pre-onset baselines for all four onset signals, so their restoration is a direct, measurable confirmation that H1 is the origin and that mitigation worked.

recommended_actions.action: Add a query-review/index gate in CI for portfolio-service (and all ledger-db callers) that requires an index-backed plan for new queries against large tables such as trades before release, mirroring the HIST-111 resolution 'Added index; query review gate'.
recommended_actions.rationale: The deploy explicitly carried 'no migration included' for a new query on a 48.2M-row table; the same failure mode previously caused HIST-111. A release-time gate prevents recurrence on the shared ledger-db instance.

recommended_actions.action: Instrument ledger-db so DB-side index and plan behaviour is observable (index_scans/seq_scans, pg_stat_user_indexes/index size, lock waits, IOPS/dish latency, and autovacuum/dead-tuple activity), and extend log retention beyond the current 05:00Z floor.
recommended_actions.rationale: ledger-db exposes only connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min and no catalog/index telemetry, which is exactly why the 'new query vs plan regression' sub-detail could not be proven; log retention capped at 05:00Z also prevented a true pre-deploy baseline. Closing these gaps makes the next incident decidable in minutes.

recommended_actions.action: Resolve the CPU/IO-vs-pooled-connection sub-detail as a follow-up: obtain ledger-db max_connections and the configured pool sizes for the four callers, and confirm whether a pooler sits in front of ledger-db. Ledger-db showed ~190-199 active connections at onset against two observed ~50-connection caller pools.
recommended_actions.rationale: No pooler node appears in the topology, no max_connections/pool_size key exists in the change record, and per-service config lookups returned count 0, so the binding shared resource could not be measured. This determines whether future remediation should also include pooler/limit tuning, but does not change the origin or the fix above.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT revert or further tune the ledger-db autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor change (cfg-2903) as an incident mitigation; leave it at 0.1 and instead confirm on the next occurrence that no vacuum line touches trades.
recommended_actions.rationale: Autovacuum activity on ledger-db is entirely on public.audit_log, cadence is unchanged before/after 08:00Z, there is no vacuum event near onset, and the config change precedes onset by ~48-56 minutes across a flat gap; reverting it would not address the observed pressure and would discard an intentional DBA change for no benefit.

recommended_actions.action: Check payment-service and settlement-service (the other two ledger-db callers) at the app layer for the same 08:45-09:00Z onset, and confirm there was no order-service pod restart at 08:5xZ (memory_pct/restarts).
recommended_actions.rationale: Blast radius on the shared ledger-db is asserted from topology, not measured — payment-service and settlement-service were never checked, and portfolio-service degraded in latency only (error_rate flat ~0.2%). Completing this bounds the true impact and closes the last untested H4 variant (a restart at onset).

data_gaps: ledger-db's literal index inventory for trades(account_id, executed_at) could not be read: the datastore exposes only connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min, and no tool exposes pg_indexes/pg_stat_user_indexes/EXPLAIN. This is why H1's first hop (new query vs plan regression) remains an assumption and confidence is capped at 0.72 rather than high.

No pre-deploy baseline for the trades query pattern exists: the log store retains only from 2026-05-05T05:00:00Z, so the requested 2026-05-01 to 05:00Z index-DDL sweep could not actually run and a plan change at 08:56Z cannot be compared against earlier plan shapes.

ledger-db max_connections could not be retrieved (no config entry exists and no server-settings endpoint is exposed), so it is unknown whether the observed ~190-199 active connections at onset is near or well below the server ceiling — the core numeric discriminator between CPU/IO saturation and connection/pool saturation.

Configured per-service pool sizes for order-service and portfolio-service were not obtainable (both per-service config lookups returned count 0, and no pool_size-like key appears in any config change), so pool utilization ratios and headroom could not be computed.

Pooler presence in front of ledger-db is unverified either way: the topology shows only direct db edges from four services with no pooler node, but absence from topology is not proof of absence in reality.

order-service memory_pct and restarts were never retrieved (budget exhausted), so a restart-driven variant of H4 (order-service pod restart at onset) remains unchecked. order-service also emits no GC-pause, heap, thread-pool or worker metric, so H4 cannot be disproven via those curves.
payment-service and settlement-service, the other two ledger-db db-callers, were never checked at the app layer, so blast radius beyond order-service and portfolio-service is not corroborated.

No vacuum/autovacuum, lock-wait, checkpoint/IO or IOPS metric exists on ledger-db, so H2's mechanism could not be tested at the metric level (it was closed on log evidence and timing instead) and H3's storage-throttling mechanism could not be directly confirmed or excluded.
order-service and ledger-db log queries were truncated (284/360 matched, 30 returned), so rarer error signatures beyond the top pattern (e.g. connection timeout, lock wait) were not fully enumerated.

The fallback check for any index-scan plan anywhere in 2026-05-01 through 2026-05-05 was not completed (budget exhausted on the 'Index Scan', 'REINDEX' and 'trades' log searches and on an index-scan metric query, which failed not_found).
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Discovery that trades(account_id, executed_at) already had a usable index before 08:56Z, or evidence in the logs/catalog that the plan changed from Index Scan to Seq Scan at 08:56Z — this would shift the origin from 'v4.5.0 introduced a new unindexed query' to 'plan regression / lost index at the same moment' (same origin, same fix family, but would change the long-term prevention emphasis).
Discovery that portfolio-service's trades query existed before v4.5.0 and was already Seq-Scanning at volume — this would break the causal link to the deploy and weaken H1 substantially.

Evidence of a storage/host/infrastructure event on the ledger-db host (IOPS throttling, volume burst-credit exhaustion, disk-latency spike, or a maintenance entry outside the deployment/config APIs) at the 08:48-08:56Z onset — this would revive H3 and could displace H1 as the origin.

A ledger-db autovacuum, lock, or bloat event on the trades table at 08:56-08:58Z (or slowing of queries on trades concurrent with vacuum runs) — this would revive H2 and contradict the log-based closure.

Evidence that order-service's own CPU, memory, restarts, thread pool or a pre-onset db_pool saturation degraded BEFORE the 08:45-08:56Z bucket — this would revive H4 and make order-service a contributor rather than a pure victim.

Confirmation that order-service writes and portfolio-service reads do NOT contend on the same ledger-db budget (e.g. separate instances, a pooler isolating them, or writes going to a different node) — this would break the second load-bearing hop of H1 and require re-attributing the order-service timeouts.

Confirmation of a pooler in front of ledger-db plus a known max_connections much lower than ~199 — this would move the binding resource from CPU/IO to connections and shift remediation toward pooler/limit tuning (origin and primary fix unchanged).

Any evidence that the order-service statement timeouts are client-side (connection-timeout/pool-exhaustion errors of the HIST-115 type) rather than server-side CPU/IO starvation — this would change the mechanism attribution and the remediation.

Evidence that payment-service and/or settlement-service show the same onset with error rates, or that portfolio-service's 5xx also rose — this would widen the measured blast radius and further support the shared-ledger-db saturation mechanism.

findings.statement: ledger-db replication_lag_ms stayed flat at ~39-41ms across the whole window (min 36.05, max 43.67) with no change at onset, so replication lag is NOT part of the degradation.

Change inventory for the window is exactly two entries and both are confirmed by independent re-query: one deployment (portfolio-service v4.5.0 at 2026-05-05T08:56:00Z, changes include 'new query on trades filtered by account_id + executed_at', 'no migration included', status 'live', rolled_back_at null) and one config change (ledger-db autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2 -> 0.1 at 2026-05-05T08:00:00Z by dba-team, 'More aggressive autovacuum'). No order-service release exists in the window, matching the report.

No other changes exist as a candidate: the preceding 18h sweep (2026-05-04T12:00Z to 2026-05-05T06:00Z) returned count 0 for deployments and count 0 for config changes, so the autovacuum change (08:00Z) and portfolio-service v4.5.0 (08:56Z) are the only two changes on the board.

Timing alignment: onset of all four first-rising samples (order-service p99, error_rate, ledger-db CPU/connections/slow_queries) is the 08:48-08:56Z bucket, i.e. the autovacuum change at 08:00Z precedes onset by ~48-56min with a long flat gap, whereas the portfolio-service deployment is timestamped 08:56:00Z, inside the onset bucket itself, and the first DB-side slow query (portfolio-service Seq Scan on trades) is 08:58:38Z, one bucket after. So the deployment aligns tightly with onset; the autovacuum change does not align in time, only in ordering (it is earlier).

Concurrent-change question is answered structurally: ledger-db is a shared postgres with four direct db callers (order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service, settlement-service) and shared=true, so a ledger-db-side slowdown can hit all four. The only service-side change in the window is on portfolio-service, which is one of those four callers -- meaning the change and the shared bottleneck are on the same dependency path, not independent coincidences.

order-service's dependency surface contains no other changed node: its edges are ledger-db (db), pricing-engine (http), exchange-gateway (http) and kafka (queue-produce); the shared components on this path are ledger-db and kafka, and no deployment/config edge for order-service exists in the window, consistent with it having no release this week.

Precedent search for autovacuum returns nothing: a targeted query for 'autovacuum table bloat vacuum settings slowdown ledger-db' returns only HIST-110 (2026-01-15, ledger-db IOPS throttling, symptoms 'order latency','statement timeouts','slow queries'), HIST-111 (2025-05-22, 'New report query without index did sequential scans', services ledger-db+settlement-service, resolution 'Added index'), HIST-102 and HIST-114 -- no incident mentions autovacuum as a cause. findings.statement: The earliest ANY 'SELECT * FROM trades ... Seq Scan on trades' line is 2026-05-05T08:58:38Z. A targeted query for 'Seq Scan' restricted to 06:00:00Z-08:58:39Z returned total_matched=1, the 08:58:38Z line only; before that instant there are ZERO such lines. So ZERO Seq Scan lines occurred BEFORE 08:56:00Z.

Per-minute counts of the portfolio-service Seq Scan line: before 08:56:00Z = 0 across every minute in 06:00-08:56Z. After deploy: 08:58Z=1, 08:59Z=2, 09:00Z=4, 09:01Z=4, 09:02Z=3, 09:03Z=3, 09:04Z=3, 09:05Z=2, 09:06Z=4, 09:07Z=2, 09:08Z=3, 09:09Z=5, 09:10Z=1 (report time), 09:11Z=3 — i.e. the line immediately switches from absent to a steady multi-per-minute plateau from 08:58Z onward. total 360 over ~120min after onset.

Plan-change evidence in the logs is that the plan shape is STABLE (same 'Seq Scan on trades (rows=48211907)' in every one of the 360 lines, before and after onset) — there is no logged line showing a plan CHANGE (e.g. an Index Scan before and a Seq Scan after), and no index name and no DDL/index-creation line was logged. A query for INFO lines containing 'index' over 06:00-11:00Z returned total_matched=0. So the logs neither display an index on trades(account_id, executed_at) being used nor show one being created/removed; there is no pre-08:56 baseline occurrence of this query pattern to compare plan shape against, because the query appears (and is already Seq Scan) only from 08:58:38Z — consistent with a new query arriving with the deploy.

Autovacuum activity on ledger-db is entirely on public.audit_log, NOT on trades: all 20 'autovacuum: processed table public.audit_log' INFO lines (first 06:30:57Z, last 10:55:51Z) name audit_log; no autovacuum line, lock, or bloat signal mentions 'trades'. The only non-autovacuum INFO line is 'config change cfg-2903 applied: autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor=0.1' at 08:00:20Z. autovacuum run cadence is similar before and after 08:00Z (e.g. 07:41:30Z, 07:34:35Z, 07:26:03Z vs 08:08:06Z, 08:20:25Z, 08:28:13Z), and there is no autovacuum event at 08:56-08:58Z.

No autovacuum/verbose WARN activity exists on ledger-db in the pre-onset window: WARN logs 06:00:00-08:56:00Z returned total_matched=1, a single unrelated 'clock drift 38ms detected, resyncing with NTP' at 06:44:41Z — so there is NO autovacuum-induced lock, bloat, or slow-query WARN before 08:56Z, and no autovacuum log activity temporally coincides with the Seq Scans. Autovacuum does not align with either onset (08:56Z) or the first Seq Scan (08:58:38Z).

portfolio-service db_pool_in_use rose in the same bucket and pinned hard at its 50-connection ceiling: ~11.9-12.2 flat until 08:30Z, then avg 17.06 / max 50 at 08:45Z and exactly avg=50 max=50 for every bucket 09:00Z through 10:45Z; its CPU_pct stayed flat at ~35.5-36.6% throughout. findings.statement: ledger-db's dependency graph contains NO connection pooler, proxy or middleware node: its neighbours are exactly four direct db callers (order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service, settlement-service) plus api-gateway -> order-service/portfolio-service/payment-service http edges. ledger-db is typed 'postgres', shared=true, and each calling service has a DIRECT 'kind':'db' edge into it — there is no intermediate pgBouncer-type hop in the topology. This is absence of a documented pooler, not proof that none exists.

Per-service config lookups for the two implicated callers returned zero changes: portfolio-service count=0 and order-service count=0 for 2026-05-05T06:00-11:00Z. No pool-size setting for either service appears anywhere in the change record, so the configured pool-size denominator for order-service and portfolio-service is not obtainable from config history.

The only client-side pool capacity visible in telemetry is per-caller, not a shared denominator: portfolio-service's pool pinned at exactly its 50-connection ceiling (avg=50 max=50 for every bucket 09:00-10:45Z) and order-service's pool sat at ~44.9-46.5 with max 51.63, i.e. two independent 50-ish client pools against ledger-db, which showed ~190-199 active connections at onset. A single caller pool of 50 cannot by itself account for ~190-199 server-side connections, consistent with four callers connecting directly (no shared pooler denominator).

Precedent lead only (not evidence about this incident): searching for connection-pool history returned HIST-115 (2025-09-25) 'order-service connection pool misconfiguration', symptoms 'connection is not available','request timed out','pool exhausted', 'Datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile', resolution 'Reverted config'. This is a client-pool-size incident, the opposite side of the ledger-db-capacity question, and no returned incident documents ledger-db max_connections or a pooler.

findings.statement: ledger-db has NO catalog/index telemetry at all: its entire available_metrics list is exactly ['connections_active','cpu_pct','disk_used_pct','replication_lag_ms','slow_queries_per_min'] — there is no index_scans, seq_scans, tuples_read, pg_stat_user_indexes or index-size metric, so DB-side index usage cannot be measured on this datastore by any metric query.

No pg_indexes/EXPLAIN/catalog endpoint output exists for ledger-db; the index question 'does trades have an index on (account_id, executed_at)' is unanswerable from the available telemetry because the datastore exposes metrics and WARN/INFO log text only, and no tool returned a schema/catalog object.

Zero index-maintenance evidence exists on ledger-db for the whole incident window: a targeted INFO log search for 'index' over 06:00-11:00Z returned total_matched=0, and a wider 2026-05-01 to 2026-05-05T11:00Z search for 'index' also returned total_matched=0. There is no CREATE INDEX, DROP INDEX or REINDEX line anywhere in five days of ledger-db INFO logs.

Index DDL is explicitly absent in 06:00-11:00Z: two separate searches in that window — contains='CREATE INDEX' (tc-049) and contains='INDEX' (tc-050) — each returned total_matched=0 with truncated:false, so no index was created or dropped at or around 08:56Z and nothing in the logs shows the plan regressed at 08:56Z rather than the query being new.

Combined with the team's F22/F23/F24, the DB-side evidence is consistent with a NEW query rather than a pre-existing query whose plan regressed: the Seq Scan pattern is absent before 08:56:00Z (zero Seq Scan lines 06:00-08:58:39Z other than the single 08:58:38Z first occurrence) and is never logged as an Index Scan before and Seq Scan after — no plan-change transition is recorded anywhere.

Caveat on the zero-count results: all ledger-db log queries in this task reported data_range start '2026-05-05T05:00:00Z' — i.e. the log store only holds from 05:00Z on 2026-05-05 — so the five-day 'index' search (tc-060) could not actually scan 2026-05-01 to 05:00Z, meaning an index created or dropped before 05:00Z on 2026-05-05 would not appear.
